item.title: How AI drones are influencing the course of the Ukraine war
item.description: Artificial intelligence is making drones faster and more capable. Russia and Ukraine both use AI-powered drones, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that AI could lead decisions on the battlefield as soon as next year.
item.content:encoded:
Artificial intelligence is making drones faster and more capable. Russia and Ukraine both use AI-powered drones, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that AI could lead decisions on the battlefield as soon as next year.

(Image credit: Paula Bronstein/for NPR)

item.title: Tariffs, diesel and computer chips are driving up costs for automakers
item.description: American auto companies say they are paying more for key components like computer chips, steel and copper — plus the fuel needed to transport their products.

item.title: Their colleges closed, but the government refuses to erase their debts, lawsuit says
item.description: Federal law requires the Education Department to erase the student loans of borrowers whose colleges close suddenly. A new lawsuit claims the department isn't fully following those rules.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Spain reckons with 2nd deadly train crash of the year ahead of national election
item.description: Spain's second high-speed rail disaster this year, a crash in which one train struck another from behind, killing 68 people, has raised fresh concerns about the safety of the country's rail network.

item.title: Brewers beat the Rays to win the first World Series title in franchise history
item.description: The small-ball Milwaukee Brewers playing in the smallest market in the majors are World Series champions for the first time. The championship comes in the 58th season for a franchise that began as the Seattle Pilots in 1969.
